definition.simple: Atomic mass is basically how heavy an atom is. We compare its weight to a specific piece of a carbon atom.
definition.academic: The relative atomic mass of the atom of an element is defined as the average mass of the atom, as compared to 1/12th the mass of one carbon-12 atom.

examples: Atomic mass of Hydrogen is 1 u.
Atomic mass of Oxygen is 16 u.

common_misconceptions: Atomic mass is exactly equal to the number of protons and neutrons combined (it's actually an average).
Atomic mass is measured in grams (it's measured in unified atomic mass units, u).
ai_context.tutor_hint: Use the analogy of a fruit seller using a watermelon as a standard weight to explain relative atomic mass.
